package main

// The duplicate-key-with-another-value corpus (RB9-F6 TS port, step 3; review V-Q D1, a duplicated "transactionBlacklist" key: Go ORs the bits of AllowedTransactions
// across the occurrences of the key onto one pointer, the verifier replaced the mask with the last list). The sweeps so far wrote a WRONGLY typed value before a
// member (objsweep), a null (objsweep dup-null-after, nulldup), or a copy of the member's own value (bytes dupsame): none wrote a second value of the RIGHT type that
// differs from the first, and encoding/json does not replace in every case - it decodes the second occurrence INTO what the first made: a struct has its members
// merged, a map takes the entries, a slice has its existing elements decoded into (an element keeps the members the second occurrence does not name, and the slice is
// cut to the second one's length), and a type with its own UnmarshalJSON does what that does (AllowedTransactions Sets the bits it names onto the pointer it is given).
//
// EVERY member of EVERY object path class of the bases (the first sweepK documents of each form that hold the class, the genesis-link documents first) is given a
// second occurrence of its key, written before the member and after it, with each of the right-typed values that differ from the member's own:
//
//	array   [] ; [first element] ; [last element] ; [{}] and [{first member of the first element}] when the elements are objects
//	object  {} ; {first member} ; {last member}
//	string  "" ; the string with its first character changed
//	number  0 ; 1 ; 2
//	bool    the other value
//
// and, for the first of those values, the key in upper case after the member (encoding/json matches a key without regard to case). A case is a list of byte edits of
// the base file, judged as every byte corpus is; each shard is its own file, bytes-cases-dupdiff-<i>.json.gz, consumed by test/s3-bytes-dupdiff-<i+1>.test.ts.
//
//	XTS_SHARD=<i>/<n> ./xtsgen -fixtures $S3 -out <dir> dupdiff      (XTS_COUNT=1 only counts)

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

type rawMember struct {
	key string
	val string
}

func rawMembers(raw []byte) []rawMember {
	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
	if _, err := dec.Token(); err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	var out []rawMember
	for dec.More() {
		kt, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return nil
		}
		k, _ := kt.(string)
		var v json.RawMessage
		if err := dec.Decode(&v); err != nil {
			return nil
		}
		kb, _ := json.Marshal(k)
		out = append(out, rawMember{string(kb), string(v)})
	}
	return out
}

func rawElems(raw []byte) []string {
	var l []json.RawMessage
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &l); err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]string, len(l))
	for i, e := range l {
		out[i] = string(e)
	}
	return out
}

func flipFirst(s string) string {
	if s == "" {
		return "x"
	}
	c := s[0]
	switch {
	case c == '0':
		c = '1'
	case c == 'a':
		c = 'b'
	default:
		c = '0'
	}
	return string(c) + s[1:]
}

type dupAlt struct{ name, text string }

func dupAlts(doc []byte, n objNode) []dupAlt {
	raw := doc[n.vs:n.ve]
	var out []dupAlt
	switch n.kind {
	case 'a':
		out = append(out, dupAlt{"empty-list", "[]"})
		el := rawElems(raw)
		if len(el) > 0 {
			out = append(out, dupAlt{"first-element", "[" + el[0] + "]"})
		}
		if len(el) > 1 {
			out = append(out, dupAlt{"last-element", "[" + el[len(el)-1] + "]"})
		}
		if len(el) > 0 && strings.HasPrefix(el[0], "{") {
			out = append(out, dupAlt{"one-empty-object", "[{}]"})
			if ms := rawMembers([]byte(el[0])); len(ms) > 0 {
				out = append(out, dupAlt{"first-element-first-member", "[{" + ms[0].key + ":" + ms[0].val + "}]"})
			}
		}
	case 'o':
		out = append(out, dupAlt{"empty-object", "{}"})
		if ms := rawMembers(raw); len(ms) > 0 {
			out = append(out, dupAlt{"first-member", "{" + ms[0].key + ":" + ms[0].val + "}"})
			if len(ms) > 1 {
				l := ms[len(ms)-1]
				out = append(out, dupAlt{"last-member", "{" + l.key + ":" + l.val + "}"})
			}
		}
	case 's':
		var s string
		if json.Unmarshal(raw, &s) != nil {
			return nil
		}
		out = append(out, dupAlt{"empty-string", `""`})
		if f, _ := json.Marshal(flipFirst(s)); string(f) != string(raw) {
			out = append(out, dupAlt{"first-char-changed", string(f)})
		}
	case 'n':
		for _, v := range []string{"0", "1", "2"} {
			if v != string(raw) {
				out = append(out, dupAlt{"number-" + v, v})
			}
		}
	case 't':
		if string(raw) == "true" {
			out = append(out, dupAlt{"false", "false"})
		} else {
			out = append(out, dupAlt{"true", "true"})
		}
	}
	return out
}

func dupDiffCases(doc []byte, n objNode) []objCase {
	if n.inArray || n.ms < 0 {
		return nil
	}
	key := string(doc[n.ms:n.vs]) // `"key" :` as spelled, with its colon and spacing
	var out []objCase
	for i, a := range dupAlts(doc, n) {
		out = append(out, objCase{"dup-" + a.name + "-before", []ByteEdit{{n.ms, 0, ins(key + a.text + ",")}}})
		out = append(out, objCase{"dup-" + a.name + "-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + a.text)}}})
		if i == 0 && !strings.Contains(key, `\`) && strings.ToUpper(key) != key {
			out = append(out, objCase{"dup-" + a.name + "-after-upper", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + strings.ToUpper(key) + a.text)}}})
		}
	}
	// three occurrences: what a slice keeps when a null, an empty list or a shorter list comes between two lists (the slots past the length are not cleared, a null and an
	// empty list start a new slice), and what a null does between the members of an object
	raw := doc[n.vs:n.ve]
	switch n.kind {
	case 'a':
		el := rawElems(raw)
		if len(el) > 0 {
			out = append(out, objCase{"dup-null-then-first-element-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + "null," + key + "[" + el[0] + "]")}}})
		}
		if len(el) > 1 {
			regrow := "[" + strings.Repeat("{},", len(el)-1) + "{}]"
			out = append(out,
				objCase{"dup-truncate-then-regrow-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + "[{}]," + key + regrow)}}},
				objCase{"dup-empty-then-regrow-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + "[]," + key + regrow)}}},
				objCase{"dup-null-then-regrow-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + "null," + key + regrow)}}},
				objCase{"dup-truncate-then-original-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + "[" + el[0] + "]," + key + string(raw))}}})
		}
	case 'o':
		if ms := rawMembers(raw); len(ms) > 0 {
			out = append(out,
				objCase{"dup-null-then-first-member-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + "null," + key + "{" + ms[0].key + ":" + ms[0].val + "}")}}},
				objCase{"dup-null-then-original-after", []ByteEdit{{n.ve, 0, ins("," + key + "null," + key + string(raw))}}})
		}
	}
	return out
}

func dupDiffCorpus(fixtures, out string) error {
	f := &ByteFile{Format: "certen-sdk/s3-bytes-corpus/v1",
		Description: "Every member of every object path class of the bases (the first sweepK documents of each form holding the class; the genesis-link documents first), given a second occurrence of its key before and after it with each right-typed value that differs from its own (an empty list, one element, an empty object, one member, another string, number or bool), and the key in upper case after it: encoding/json decodes the second occurrence into what the first made (structs merge, maps take the entries, slices decode into their elements) and a type with its own UnmarshalJSON does what that does (AllowedTransactions ORs its bits). Judged by VerifyPortable from the text."}
	gb, err := genesisBases(fixtures)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	ob, err := objBases(fixtures)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	have := map[string]bool{}
	var bases []string
	for _, b := range append(append([]string(nil), gb...), ob...) {
		if !have[b] {
			have[b] = true
			bases = append(bases, b)
		}
	}
	f.Bases = bases
	docs := make([][]byte, len(bases))
	for bi, bpath := range bases {
		raw, err := baseDoc(fixtures, bpath)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", bpath, err)
		}
		docs[bi] = raw
		be, ok := judgeStableCounting(raw, new(int), new(int))
		if !ok {
			return fmt.Errorf("%s: Go is unstable on the base document", bpath)
		}
		f.BaseExpect = append(f.BaseExpect, be)
	}
	shard, shards := 0, 1
	if v := os.Getenv("XTS_SHARD"); v != "" {
		if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d/%d", &shard, &shards); err != nil || shards < 1 || shard < 0 || shard >= shards {
			return fmt.Errorf("XTS_SHARD %q: want i/n", v)
		}
	}
	use := map[string]int{}
	classes := map[string]bool{}
	byV := map[string]int{}
	seq := 0
	for bi, bpath := range bases {
		form := "2.1"
		if objForm20.Match(docs[bi]) {
			form = "2.0"
		}
		w := &objWalker{b: docs[bi]}
		w.value(0, "", "", -1, false)
		seen := map[string]bool{}
		for _, n := range w.out {
			if n.class == "" {
				n.class = "$root"
			}
			if seen[n.class] {
				continue
			}
			seen[n.class] = true
			k := form + "|" + n.class
			if use[k]++; use[k] > sweepK {
				continue
			}
			for _, c := range dupDiffCases(docs[bi], n) {
				if seq++; (seq-1)%shards != shard {
					continue
				}
				classes[k] = true
				if os.Getenv("XTS_COUNT") != "" {
					continue
				}
				text := applyEdits(docs[bi], c.edits)
				lastPanic, lastFlaky = "", ""
				ex, ok := judgeSweep(text, &f.Skipped.Panics, &f.Skipped.Flaky)
				if !ok {
					fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "PANIC/FLAKY %s %s [%s] %s%s\n", bpath, n.class, c.name, lastPanic, lastFlaky)
					continue
				}
				byV[ex.V]++
				f.Cases = append(f.Cases, ByteCase{ID: fmt.Sprintf("dupdiff:%s:%s:%s", bpath, n.class, c.name), Base: bi, Op: "dupdiff " + c.name, Edits: c.edits, Expect: ex})
			}
		}
	}
	var names []string
	for k, v := range byV {
		names = append(names, fmt.Sprintf("%s=%d", k, v))
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "dupdiff shard %d/%d: %d bases, %d path classes (form|class), %d cases in all, %d judged here (%s)\n", shard, shards, len(bases), len(classes), seq, len(f.Cases), strings.Join(names, " "))
	if os.Getenv("XTS_COUNT") != "" {
		return nil
	}
	return writeGz(filepath.Join(out, fmt.Sprintf("bytes-cases-dupdiff-%d.json.gz", shard)), mustJSON(f))
}
